Desktop select checkbox re-pinned. Taken clean: 014 released at b4dc64bb4e72 and the stylesheet had not moved since. Two edits planned — the main-item cell's thumb target, and the sheet grab band the outstanding list records as unowned.

Record sheet's grab band stopped at its own header. That sheet pads its top by --db-space-6, four times the menu sheets, so its bar sits 24px down and a band centred on it ran 2..50px from the sheet's top edge while the header starts at 32. Measured consequence: the band answered every press aimed at the title, and both 44px header actions delivered 26px. The title's rename opens on a double-click, so the second tap never reached it — which is why renaming looked as though tap-to-open had removed it from the phone. Band now runs from the sheet's top edge to the bottom of the handle's own margin box: 35px, 0 stolen, title reachable, both actions 44 of 44, and a real double-tap on the title renames again. Menu sheets keep the shared rule unchanged and were measured at 41px with 0 stolen before and after. The band is an invisible pseudo-element, so this is a hit-testing change only: screenshots of both sheet surfaces are byte-identical with the override on and off.

Main-item cell touch target: tried and reverted, byte-identically. A downward negative-inset pseudo-element to lift the 169x34 cell to the 44px floor is a measured no-op here for two independent reasons — the cell clips its overflow, so the pseudo-element is cut back to the cell box (the last row gained 0px), and in a contiguous table the next row's own area begins exactly where this one's box ends, so there are no dead pixels to reclaim. Only row height reaches 44 and that is a density setting. Reverted rather than shipped, since a rule that measures as a no-op advertises a fix that is not there. Replaced by a check that measures the reach and asserts the property that IS achievable: no press lands on the wrong row.

One block added, nothing else touched: removing it returns styles.css to b4dc64bb4e72 byte for byte. Four switch repairs, each measured. (1) The display-style popover redeclared the whole switch under its own ancestor - the last live rule in the stylesheet handing a checkbox its appearance from where it was mounted, and a copy that had drifted to a weaker border and a knob taken from the surface fill. Deleted; that popover inherits the one definition. Unguarded ancestor-keyed appearance rules 1 -> 0. (2) The switch radius read a token with no literal fallback, so a portalled switch computed 0px and the pill became a square: 9999px inside the container, 0px outside, now identical. (3) Alignment for three switch rows de-scoped off .note-database-container onto the row that travels with the control. (2) and (3) together: toggles losing a computed property when moved out of the container 10/10 -> 0/10, each half shown failing again on its own. (4) The switch was reachable at 34x18 under this phase's 28px floor; a coarse-pointer ::after band takes it to 34x28 with the painted box unchanged, so no desktop capture moves.

The reorder button and the row checkbox stopped overlapping. Three rules fought over that button and the touch-floor block won something that was not its business: it opened with display:inline-flex, the same weight as the display:none written for these buttons off a phone and later in the file, so a minimum-size rule decided that a phone-only control renders in every desktop list and gallery row, unstyled. Display removed from the floor block; the floor kept. The column was then re-derived: its own comment read 48 = button 24 + checkbox 16 + gap 8, and both controls have since grown to 28 for the touch floor while the column stayed at 48. 4 + 28 + 4 + 28 = 64, matched in getSelectionColumnWidth's touch branch, with the phone pin 6px -> 4px and the phone button declared at the 28px it has been painting all along. Measured gap between the two controls: desktop -17px -> no button rendered at all, which is what production does since the table creates it only on touch; phone -14px in a 49px cell -> +4px in a 65px cell.

The sheet grab band still falls short of the operator's 48px, and now the reason is measured rather than guessed. The theft is fixed — the record sheet's band no longer covers its own title or the top 18px of its two 44px actions — but the band is 35px on the record sheet and 41px on the owned-menu sheet, because that is all the chrome those sheets have above their first content: 33px and 40px respectively. 48px of exclusive drag band does not fit above either header. Closing it means making the sheet header taller, which moves every sheet's content and every capture of it, or per-surface overrides that each claim their own free space. Both are visual decisions for the operator; verify-placement pins the current numbers either way.

--text-muted on the plugin's own panel measures 4.1:1 in the light capture theme at 12px, below the 4.5:1 floor for body text. It is the token .db-menu-section, .db-add-view-field-label and every muted caption in the plugin share, so this is a program-wide decision rather than one surface's. Dark measures 4.89:1 and passes.

The select-column appearance block (border, accent fill, custom checkmark) is still guarded :not(the shared checkbox class) and is therefore dead code, as are the equivalent modal and CSV-option blocks. The shared component supplies all of it, so nothing is visibly missing — but three dead blocks remain in the sheet and the next reader will believe they are live. Removing them is a separate, capture-affecting change.

DECLINED, with the shortfall stated: the table's main-item cell measures 169x34 against WCAG 2.5.5 AAA's 44px (40px at the loosest density). The operator chose density - row height stays at 34px and no phone-only override is added, because raising it would override the reader's own density setting, which is a deliberate preference. WCAG 2.5.8 AA's 24px floor is met. verify-placement reports the 33px reach on every run, so the number stays visible rather than being closed by silence.

The list roving-tabindex selector at src/views/card-roving-tabindex.ts:313 queries .db-card-field, .db-gallery-card-field and .db-list-row-field. None of the three is built or styled anywhere: the renderers pass db-board-card-field, db-gallery-field and db-list-field. Not a behaviour defect - card-field-renderer.ts sets data-note-database-column-key and role=gridcell on every field, and the selector's other two arms match through those - so the three names are dead weight rather than broken navigation. Found while closing the row matrix's invented classes and left alone: it is outside 005's scope, and the same rot in one more place is worth recording rather than folding into an unrelated diff.
